title: Incapacity for work in professional fire departments in North Rhine-Westphalia: An empirical analysis of patterns and associated factors as a basis for developing setting-specific prevention strategies
summary:
Background

Incapacity for work is an important health and occupational issue among members of professional fire departments. However, there is still limited knowledge about which health problems are most commonly associated with incapacity for work in professional fire departments in North Rhine-Westphalia, which work-related and individual factors may play a role, and which preventive measures are already used or may additionally be needed.

Research questions

The study investigates which patterns of incapacity for work are perceived by members of professional fire departments in North Rhine-Westphalia. This includes the frequency and duration of incapacity for work as well as commonly reported patterns of illness. The findings will also be compared with available data from the general population. In addition, the study examines which work-related and individual factors are perceived by fire department members as being associated with incapacity for work. Further questions address the use and perceived effectiveness of existing preventive measures and the need for additional measures. Based on these findings, suitable prevention approaches tailored to the specific conditions of professional fire departments are to be developed.

Methods

The study consists of three consecutive stages. First, members of professional fire departments are interviewed individually about their experiences and perceptions. This is followed by an anonymous online survey among members of professional fire departments in North Rhine-Westphalia. In the third stage, experts from relevant professional fields are interviewed to provide expert interpretation of the findings from the previous stages and to assess and further develop possible preventive measures. Finally, the findings from all three stages are integrated and analyzed.
conditions: Incapacity for work among civil servants employed in professional fire departments in North Rhine-Westphalia. The study examines the frequency and duration of incapacity for work as well as subjectively perceived patterns of illness, particularly musculoskeletal disorders, respiratory diseases, mental disorders, injuries, cardiovascular diseases, and diseases of the digestive system.

interventions.name: Civil servants employed in professional fire departments in North Rhine-Westphalia are interviewed once in an approximately 55-minute semi-structured interview using an interview guide on incapacity for work, associated factors, and prevention.

Civil servants employed in professional fire departments in North Rhine-Westphalia participate once in an approximately 15-minute standardized anonymous online survey on incapacity for work, associated factors, and prevention.

Experts from relevant professional fields are interviewed once in an approximately 55-minute semi-structured interview using an interview guide to interpret the study findings and assess prevention needs and potential prevention approaches for professional fire departments.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Stage 1
- Civil servant employed in a professional fire department in North Rhine-Westphalia
- Completion of the probationary period
- Occupational duties within the scope of the relevant North Rhine-Westphalia legislation on fire protection, emergency assistance, civil protection, and emergency medical services (BHKG NRW and RettG NRW)
- At least five years of professional experience
- Voluntary participation and written informed consent after provision of study information

Stage 2
- Civil servant employed in a professional fire department in North Rhine-Westphalia
- Completion of the probationary period
- Occupational duties within the scope of the relevant North Rhine-Westphalia legislation on fire protection, emergency assistance, civil protection, and emergency medical services (BHKG NRW and RettG NRW)
- At least five years of professional experience
- Voluntary participation after provision of study information; informed consent is provided by proceeding with the online survey

Stage 3
- At least five years of professional experience in a relevant professional field, particularly occupational medicine, occupational psychology, workplace health management, or executive-level leadership in a professional fire department
- Appropriate professional qualification
- Voluntary participation and written informed consent after provision of study information
Exclusion criteria:
- Failure to meet the respective inclusion criteria
- Lack of consent to participation or data processing
- Lack of consent to the use of study data
- For Stage 2 only: incomplete or clearly erroneous questionnaire datasets
